zentou_2019_monod.name: Monod
zentou_2019_monod.description: The model represents batch alcoholic fermentation of molasses by Saccharomyces cerevisiae and predicts biomass, sugar substrate, and ethanol concentrations over time. It is a compact dynamic concentration model in which substrate-dependent Monod growth is linked to substrate consumption and ethanol production through yield coefficients. Fermentation was run in a stirred, 1-L-capacity bioreactor with 250 mL of medium, initially micro-aerated and then operated anaerobically. The authors estimated the Monod growth parameters from batch data at low initial sugar concentrations and compared simulated predictions with separate experiments at initial concentrations of 75, 150, and 225 g/L. The model fit best at low substrate concentration and became less accurate at high concentration, where it does not represent substrate inhibition. The authors present it as a practical model for predicting and supporting the optimization and control of molasses fermentation under a suitable, specific range of conditions.

zentou_2019_andrews.name: Andrews
zentou_2019_andrews.description: The Andrews model describes batch alcoholic fermentation of molasses by Saccharomyces cerevisiae and predicts changes in biomass, sugar substrate, and ethanol concentration. It combines a substrate-inhibition growth law with batch balances that link substrate consumption and ethanol production to cell growth through yield coefficients. Fermentation experiments used a stirred 1-L bioreactor with a 250-mL working volume, initially micro-aerated and then run anaerobically. The Andrews parameters were estimated from growth data at high substrate concentrations, and the model was simulated with MATLAB and compared against separate batch experiments at three initial substrate concentrations. The model agreed best with the high-concentration validation data and less well with the low-concentration data; the authors present it as useful for describing fermentation within a suitable operating range, rather than as a universal model.
